speaker: Wren
current_text: Another one through the shafts. Sit. I am Wren. I was Royal Archivist, once. Now I keep the records this city is not supposed to have.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease. We are the Wrinkles: the people {villain} could not iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea is better.

speaker: Wren
current_text: He is in the castle at the north end, and he truly believes he is helping. That is the hard part. Talk to the streets. Each of them holds a piece of him.

speaker: Wren
current_text: You did it. Sit. I am Wren: Royal Archivist, and for ten years the only honest record in this city.

speaker: Wren
current_text: The Crease is just a cellar now. We are keeping it anyway, for the stories.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Thank you. I mean that more than I have ever meant a footnote.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Back in one piece? Good. Mostly one piece.

speaker: Wren
current_text: The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It makes the work harder and the ending better.
new_text: The records say he began as a good man. Keep that in mind. It does not excuse what he has done.
writer_note: Removes a prediction about the ending; preserves Wren wanting him stopped without calling him a monster.

speaker: Wren
current_text: The kingdom is mending, one argument at a time. It is dreadfully inefficient. I have never been happier. Take your time.

speaker: Wren
current_text: You brought me something from the streets. It goes in the true record, in ink, where he cannot correct it.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Two pieces of him now. A man who needs to be right. A man who cannot bear to be disagreed with. I can almost see his shape.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Three. He is afraid, you know. Not of you.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Of everything that will not obey. A small, sad fear, for a man with so much gold.

speaker: Wren
current_text: All four. I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.

speaker: Wren
current_text: He is a man who made a list of everything he could not control, and made it illegal.

speaker: Wren
current_text: Go and finish it. Gently, if you can. But finish it.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: Hesper Dray. Nurse. Sit. Drink.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: Tea. Strong, bitter and unapproved. Unapproved things heal faster. That isn't medicine. It's just true.
new_text: Tea. Strong, bitter, unapproved. Drink while it is still three things the Ministry dislikes.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: The rifts? His hold is failing. Everything he forced together keeps coming apart, and he keeps stitching.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: It began the night the boy got out, they say. Nobody says 'boy' where the loudspeakers can hear.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: Bleeding again? Sit. I'll pretend to be surprised.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: Hesper Dray. Sit. Drink.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: Still unapproved. Nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to my tea.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Shh. Keep it down. Old Fern. Composter.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: I turned this city's waste back into soil. Now that's 'untidy', and so am I. Criminally untidy. Worms in my hat to prove it.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: They shoved the rubbish behind the facade and called it 'Behind'. The land's sick. Nothing grows. Help me save what's left.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Old Fern. Composter. Allowed to say it out loud now.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: The patch came in, the heaps are steaming and nobody's hit me in a week. Untidy and proud.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Any luck? The heaps are in cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding. They're being rescued.

speaker: Old Fern
current_text: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. I might. Come back any time.
new_text: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Waste of water when I could be watering the patch. Come back any time.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Oh. A visitor. Forgive me, I've forgotten how this goes. I am Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: I cannot bury him. The permit loops: Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. So he waits in his chair. He was always the patient one.
new_text: I cannot bury him. Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. He has waited in his chair for three years.
writer_note: Removes patient-husband punchline; keeps permit loop and loss.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: I've started talking to him. He doesn't interrupt. Please, if you can help.
new_text: I talk to him in the parlour. I don't know what else to do. Please, if you can help.
writer_note: Widow Pell: plain grief, no interruption joke.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Widow Pell. My husband is at rest. I visit him every morning.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: Thank you. I will never say it enough, so I keep saying it.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: The stamp, remember. Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where nobody official would look: somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads.

speaker: Widow Pell
current_text: We're well. My husband would have said you were late. He'd have meant it fondly.
new_text: We visit every morning. I tell him about the people who helped us. I tell him about you.
writer_note: Keeps the grateful return visit without a lateness punchline.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Rollo Spokes... foreman. Beefcake. Learned the wheels... in the Gainlands. Back then, a wheel stopped at night.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Now the facade needs light... so we pedal. Free. Forever. We were told... it was cardio. My calves have calves.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Rollo Spokes. The wheels are slow, and the crews are sitting in the sun, lifting nothing. Best I've ever seen them look.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: The crews won't stop... till somebody says it's all right. You say it.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
current_text: We're lifting again. Real things. On purpose. Come and watch the crews. Bring a snack.
